edge.title: The sweets with no date on them
edge.anchor: Hindustan Times reports that Karnataka's health department shut a juice counter at a Bengaluru PVR over allegations of reused disposable cups, which PVR denies.
edge.setup: Festival week. The shop's trays are piled with bright, glossy mithai, loose, in a glass counter, no date anywhere. A box is ₹400 cheaper than the packaged brand next door and the shopkeeper says it was made fresh this morning. Everyone is buying; you have ten minutes and a house full of guests.
edge.tell: If nobody can show you a date on the tray or a food licence number on the wall, 'fresh this morning' is just a sentence.
move: Look for the best-before date on the tray or counter: FSSAI requires loose sweets to display one. No date means walk on.
Look for the shop's FSSAI licence or registration number displayed at the counter.
Prefer milk-based sweets from a high-turnover shop on a busy day over a bargain from a quiet one.
If you fall ill or find something wrong, keep the box and bill, and report it to the food safety authority through the FSSAI Food Safety Connect app.
edge.why: Freshness and safety are invisible at the counter, so the seller knows what you can't, and festival rush removes your time to check. A displayed date and licence number turn an unverifiable claim into a checkable one; an unwillingness to display them is itself the information.
edge.variants: Same shape: loose ghee and oil sold by weight, 'organic' produce with no label, street food at a mela where nothing is traceable.

lens.name: Base rates
lens.one_line: How common something is in general tells you more than how vivid this particular case is.
lens.detail: A horrifying story about one crime says nothing about whether crime rose. Your sense of risk is built almost entirely from stories, and stories are selected for how striking they are, not how typical. The corrective is boring and effective: before reacting, ask what the denominator is.
elsewhere: A startup founder's biography is a sample of one from a pool with a 90% failure rate.
A rare drug side-effect reported in the news, against how many prescriptions.
Plane crash coverage versus the per-kilometre fatality rate.
lens.test: Out of how many? If you can't name the denominator, you don't yet have information — you have an anecdote.
lens.today: Bengaluru's feeds are heavy today with the family-massacre and serial-murder coverage (The Times of India, NDTV). It is vivid and it will feel like a risk to you, but it describes one household, not the odds on your street. Your commute, the Ballari Road curbs and the Deepavali road rush are far likelier to cost you an hour, so spend your caution there.

carry_over.prompt: A small loan app starts calling your contacts and your manager after one late payment — what is the one thing about this pressure you should recognise?
carry_over.answer: The pressure is aimed at your reputation, not your bank account — which means it's outside the law, not inside it.
